html:
Chicago is the largest city of the American Midwest, on Lake Michigan in Illinois. It grew faster than almost any city of the 1800s, from a frontier fort to a city of over a million people in about sixty years.

Its site was a short portage between the Great Lakes and the Mississippi river system. Fort Dearborn was built there in 1803, and the town was founded in 1833. A canal to the Illinois River in 1848, and then railways, made it the hub where the farms and forests of the West met the cities of the East:

  • Grain from the prairie came through its elevators; Cyrus McCormick built his reapers here.
  • Cattle and hogs came to the Union Stock Yards, and its packers shipped meat across the country in refrigerated rail cars.

The Great Chicago Fire of 1871 burned the centre, and the rebuilt city put up the first steel-framed skyscrapers. Its factories drew immigrants from Germany, Ireland, Poland and Italy, and its labour struggles were fierce: the Haymarket affair of 1886 is remembered on May Day around the world. In 1893 the World's Columbian Exposition was held here, where Swami Vivekananda spoke to the Parliament of Religions.

In the 1900s the Great Migration brought hundreds of thousands of Black Southerners to its South Side, the home of Chicago blues and jazz. Walt Disney was born here, and Barack Obama began his political life here.
sum: Chicago is the largest city of the American Midwest, on Lake Michigan in Illinois. It grew faster than almost any city of the 1800s, from a frontier fort to a city of over a million people in about sixty years.
